## Initial pass: six lanes narrowed

### ET-17 and ET-18: Gartner artifact and partial comparator roster

The Gartner source is now identifiable as **“Emerging Tech: AI Vendor Race: Startups to Watch in Synthetic Population and Behavioral Simulation,” Vibha Chitkara, 14 April 2026**, document ID `7718657`. Gartner blocks public access to the full document, so the complete 33-company watch roster is not yet recovered. Public vendor reproductions establish a partial denominator without establishing Gartner endorsement:

- Electric Twin says Gartner reviewed 60 companies, selected 33 to watch, and placed Electric Twin in a `scale-up` tier.
- NewtonX says it was one of 10 `front-runners` among 60 startups.
- Stravito says it was placed in the `Front Runner` category.
- BluePill says it was placed in `Polished Diamonds`.
- Verve says it was named in the report and reproduces a Gartner description of its virtual intelligent personas, but its accessible post does not state a tier.

Sources:
- https://www.linkedin.com/posts/electric-twin_a-few-years-ago-synthetic-audiences-barely-activity-7475820150097895424-Wg-Z
- https://www.stravito.com/resources/stravito-recognized-as-a-front-runner-in-the-2026-gartner-emerging-tech-ai-vendor-race-startups-to-watch-in-synthetic-population-and-behavioral-simulation
- https://www.addverve.com/inspiration/verve-named-in-gartner-report-emerging-tech-ai-vendor-race-startups-to-watch-in-synthetic-population-and-behavioral-simulation/
- https://blue-pill.ai/blog/bluepill-is-recognized-in-the-2026-gartner-emerging-tech-ai-vendor-race-startups-to-watch-in-synthetic-population-and-behavioral-simulation-report

**Disposition:** partial positive. Freeze these five vendors as a provisional recovery set, but do not call it the Gartner roster. Continue source-complete recovery until all 33 watched companies and 60 reviewed companies are accounted for or the paywall remains an explicit denominator boundary.

### ET-06: validator and adviser chronology

Electric Twin published Michael Muthukrishna as having “recently joined” the company as a scientific adviser on 3 November 2024. LSE described him as Electric Twin’s Scientific Advisor in its June 2025 festival materials and currently describes him as Chief Science Advisor. Electric Twin’s current homepage and FAQ describe its system as independently validated by him. Companies House records Muthukrishna and Ben Warner as directors of the Centre for Human Progress from 5 August 2025.

Sources:
- https://www.electrictwin.com/blog/simulating-ourselves
- https://www.lse.ac.uk/events/lse-festival/positive-futures
- https://www.lse.ac.uk/business/consulting/experts/michael-muthukrishna
- https://www.electrictwin.com/faq
- https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/16630851/officers

**Disposition:** role overlap verified; scientific compromise not established. The remaining question is procedural: which validation occurred before or after each role, who controlled the test design and holdout data, and what “independent” meant operationally at the time of the claim.

### ET-11: ethics-board remit and government restrictions

The Civil Service Commission records Simon Case’s role as unpaid and part-time, with meetings approximately twice a year. It states that he will advise on the ethics of using AI. Through 31 March 2027, he may not use privileged information, lobby the UK Government or arm’s-length bodies for Electric Twin, use government contacts to influence policy or secure business or funding, or advise Electric Twin on a UK government bid or contract. The Commission also records his statement that he had no official dealings with Electric Twin and made no regulatory, funding, or other decisions affecting it during his final two civil-service years.

Source:
- https://civilservicecommission.independent.gov.uk/case/member-of-the-ethics-board-electric-twin/

**Disposition:** appointment and restrictions verified. No public charter, audit power, publication right, incident process, recusal procedure, or enforcement authority for the wider ethics board has yet been located. The available official record supports an advisory surface, not an independent audit body.

### ET-01 and ET-12: September 2025 financing and governance event

Companies House records the following sequence:

- Ben Blume appointed director effective 12 September 2025.
- New articles and resolutions filed 23 September, including allotment authority, variation of share rights, adoption of articles, and removal of pre-emption rights.
- Seed 2 Preferred allotments occurred on 16, 17, and 26 September 2025.
- The three allotments total 739,180 Seed 2 Preferred shares. Each SH01 reports `9.267` as the amount paid per share, which produces a derived cash figure of approximately **£6.85 million**.
- Additional allotments were filed in January, March, April, and July 2026.

Sources:
- https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/15173006/filing-history
- https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/15173006/officers

**Disposition:** the financing event and governance change are official-record positives. Do not yet equate the £6.85 million derived filing figure with the later announced $10 million round. The shareholder identities, currency conversion, closing structure, and any later tranche must be reconciled from confirmation statements, filed documents, and investor announcements.

### ET-08: The Times deployment

Electric Twin describes The Times as its first client. Its case study says the system was used across product, marketing, and commercial teams; a 10 percent holdout from a 642,000-subscriber base produced a vendor-reported 92 percent result; and synthetic testing informed the name of The Times’ business podcast. Independent trade reporting corroborates the existence of Times ExplorAItion, its use of stripped-back subscriber behaviour, reader panels, engagement and PAMCo data, and its availability to advertisers and agencies.

Sources:
- https://www.electrictwin.com/blog/the-times-announces-its-new-synthetic-audience-tool-built-on-electric-twin
- https://www.electrictwin.com/times
- https://www.research-live.com/article/news/electric-twin-and-the-times-partner-on-synthetic-audiences/id/5148966

**Disposition:** deployment verified; accuracy remains vendor/customer reported. The phrase “validated against 642,000 subscribers” must not be allowed to obscure that the company describes a 10 percent holdout and does not publicly expose question-level results, subgroup errors, or the full protocol.

### ET-10: procurement search boundary

Exact-name web-index searches of Contracts Finder and Find a Tender returned no Electric Twin or former-name notices. This is not a negative finding. Contracts Finder’s public OCDS search API filters by date and stage rather than arbitrary supplier keyword, portal indexing is incomplete, and supplier names must be searched inside bulk release data and matched against legal names, company number, former name, and trading names.

Sources:
- https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/apidocumentation
- https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/open-contracting

**Disposition:** unresolved. Build the API or bulk-data adapter before reporting any null.

## Next control

The next pass should recover the complete Gartner denominator, archive every validation claim by date, parse the September 2025 confirmation statement and articles, and run a source-complete procurement scan. Does the same evidence battery produce materially different governance, validation, and customer-use results for NewtonX, Stravito, Verve, and BluePill, or does Electric Twin mainly appear exceptional because its founders and official records are unusually visible?

## Second pass: all 18 lanes exercised, no graph promotion

Capture date: 2026-07-19. This is a receipt-level research update only. Every observation remains **graph_effect: none**, **machine_proposed_unverified**, and blocked from publication pending frozen receipts and human review. “Verified” below means the bounded official fact or public statement is addressably receipted; it does not validate product performance, operational adherence, motive, or wrongdoing.

### Strongest new result: the validation record is now classifiable

A disclosed working paper now exists: [Where You Ask Matters: Platform Effects of Online Surveys and AI-Based Human Subject Simulation](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=6439338), written 18 March and posted 1 April 2026. It compares 7,755 UK respondents across seven human-source types with an Electric Twin synthetic benchmark. The paper and cited preregistration materially improve the procedural record, but they do not provide an unaffiliated replication of Electric Twin’s headline percentages.

The paper discloses that Electric Twin funded the work; Ben Warner co-authored it and co-founded Electric Twin; Michael Muthukrishna was Electric Twin’s Science Advisor; both held shares; Stack Data Strategy conducted the commissioned fieldwork; LSE ethics approval 542028 applied; and an OSF preregistration is cited. These are positive disclosure and design controls. They also mean the named validator was not institutionally unaffiliated. That is a governance classification, not evidence of bad science.

Metric verdicts:

- **95.5% 1-MAE:** partially reproducible. Electric Twin defines the per-question rule in prose as one minus the mean absolute difference across answer-option proportions, but does not publish the raw distributions or cross-question weighting needed to recalculate 95.5%.
- **92% NDAM:** not reproducible from public material. The company says NDAM normalises distribution accuracy to zero-to-one independently of answer count, but does not publish the exact equation, clipping, weighting, aggregation, or raw outputs.
- **96% FAQ/homepage match rate, 94% human-repeat ceiling, traditional-method figures, 20% improvement, and The Times 92%:** not publicly recalculable because the exact metric/sample/question outputs, uncertainty, aggregation, or version boundary are missing.

Primary receipts: [Electric Twin methodology, 11 February 2026](https://www.electrictwin.com/blog/how-accurate-are-synthetic-audiences), [FAQ](https://www.electrictwin.com/faq), [SSRN working paper](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=6439338), [OSF registration cited by the paper](https://osf.io/6yqtu), [Muthukrishna role announcement](https://www.electrictwin.com/blog/simulating-ourselves), [LSE profile](https://www.lse.ac.uk/business/consulting/experts/michael-muthukrishna), and [Centre for Human Progress officers](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/16630851/officers).

### ET-01 to ET-04 and ET-12: corporate, public-service, origin, and capital chronology

**ET-01 — partial.** Companies House verifies incorporation as Electric Sheep Intelligence Ltd on 28 September 2023, the immediate name change to Electric Twin Ltd, Warner and Cooper as founding directors/PSCs, and their current greater-than-25-percent/no-more-than-50-percent share and voting bands. It also verifies Ben Blume’s directorship from 12 September 2025 and the September resolutions, articles, share-right variation, and Seed 2 allotments. The three Seed 2 forms report 604,294 + 86,327 + 48,559 shares at £9.267 each: mechanically **£6,849,981.06**. This is a filing-derived allotment figure, not a reconciled funding-round amount. [Profile](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/15173006), [filing history](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/15173006/filing-history), [officers](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/15173006/officers), [PSC register](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/15173006/persons-with-significant-control).

ET-01 acceptance is still open: no full hash-addressed filing manifest exists; the articles, confirmation statement, 2024 subdivision baseline, and January–July 2026 allotments still require complete parsing.

**ET-02 — partial with campaign gaps.** Warner’s Inquiry evidence bounds his Faculty/ASI Data Science role from September 2015 to September 2019, polling work at Hanbury Strategy from September to December 2019, and No. 10 service from 13 December 2019 to 18 May 2021. He says HR called his post Chief Adviser to the Prime Minister on Digital and Data, while he used Special Adviser. Official SAGE minutes establish attendance, not responsibility for all SAGE decisions. This pass did not recover a primary official receipt for a Vote Leave modelling role, a specific 2019 Conservative election-model mandate, or the claim that Warner alone established 10DS. [First Inquiry statement](https://covid19.public-inquiry.uk/documents/inq000269182-witness-statement-of-ben-warner-former-special-adviser-dated-08-09-2023/), [second statement](https://covid19.public-inquiry.uk/documents/inq000657617-witness-statement-of-dr-ben-warner-former-special-adviser-cabinet-office-dated-13-10-2025/), [SAGE 9](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/sage-minutes-coronavirus-covid-19-response-20-february-2020/sage-9-minutes-coronavirus-covid-19-response-20-february-2020).

**ET-03 — partial.** Official records identify Alex Cooper’s military honours, pre-Moonshot work in the No. 10 COVID coordination cell, and leadership of Operation Moonshot deployment/NHS Test & Trace mass testing. DHSC records his departure on 12 April 2021. Sources use title variants including Mass Testing Development Director and Director of Mass Testing. No recovered record states a precise direct reporting line or a delegated instrument that would establish authority over every testing or procurement decision. [Cabinet Office Inquiry statement](https://covid19.public-inquiry.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/10182915/INQ000528389.pdf), [DHSC business-appointment record](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/dhsc-business-appointment-rules-advice-april-to-june-2021/dhsc-business-appointment-rules-advice-april-to-june-2021).

**ET-04 — partial.** The February 2026 company post is receipted as a retrospective origin narrative: the founders say they saw decisions made with inadequate information about likely public response and later built the tool they wished existed. Contemporaneous SAGE minutes and Inquiry exhibits independently establish that behavioural response, real-time behavioural data, polling, payments, and travel data were live problems and that polling/behavioural-science machinery already existed. They do not establish in-office conception, technology/data transfer, or a causal bridge from a particular decision to the company. [Company funding/origin post](https://www.electrictwin.com/blog/electric-twin-announcing-14m-in-funding), [SAGE 7](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/sage-minutes-coronavirus-covid-19-response-13-february-2020/sage-7-minutes-coronavirus-covid-19-response-13-february-2020), [SAGE 12](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/sage-minutes-coronavirus-covid-19-response-3-march-2020/sage-12-minutes-coronavirus-covid-19-response-3-march-2020).

**ET-12 — reconciliation refused.** Electric Twin announced a $10m Atomico-led round after a $4m pre-seed, $14m total. Mercuri confirms continued participation; transaction reporting also names LocalGlobe, Marc Andreessen, and Samos Investments, with additional angels reported by journalism. Blume’s directorship is official and his Atomico partnership is public, but no reviewed receipt establishes a contractual Atomico board right or observer rights. The visible 2024 allotments derive to approximately £2.995m and September 2025 Seed 2 allotments to £6.850m. They are economically proximate to, but not the same propositions as, the announced dollar rounds. Reconciliation requires shareholder/allottee mapping, transaction documents, exchange-rate and closing dates, convertibles/fees treatment, and later allotments. [Company announcement](https://www.electrictwin.com/blog/electric-twin-announcing-14m-in-funding), [Mercuri](https://www.mercuri.vc/blog/electric-twin), [Atomico profile](https://atomico.com/team/ben-blume).

### ET-07, ET-13, and ET-16: nearest reproducibility and scope boundaries

**ET-07 — protocol narrowed by observed gaps.** A blind replication should begin only with the publicly disclosed UK and US validation populations. An unaffiliated evaluator must control the held-out questions/outcomes and preregistration; freeze sampling, quotas/weights, question wording/order/options, persona-data cutoff, model/version, prompts, stochastic settings, post-processing, exclusions, abstentions, subgroup slices, and baselines; give the vendor persona-construction data but not test questions/outcomes; require timestamped option-probability vectors before outcomes are collected; publish per-question 1-MAE and an evaluator-defined total-variation accuracy unless Electric Twin publishes an identical NDAM equation; and report raw errors, confidence intervals, country/language/subgroup/question-family slices, perturbations, temporal holdouts, malformed outputs, and abstentions. A pass is bounded to that frozen population/version; a failure does not establish intent.

**ET-13 — partial.** Public production claims include LLMs plus first-/third-party survey data, persona/evaluation separation, API-accessed underlying models, post-processing to distributions, and continuous per-question evaluation. A May 2026 Research Engineer posting names cognitive architectures, context engineering, memory, chain-of-thought prompting, RAG, and agentic tool use; those are hiring requirements/research direction, not proof of deployed features. No public source located names the foundation-model provider, prompt templates, memory store, retrieval corpus, calibration code, tool permissions, or customer-data route to a provider. [Methodology](https://www.electrictwin.com/blog/how-accurate-are-synthetic-audiences), [Research Engineer posting](https://careers.atomico.com/companies/electric-twin-2/jobs/78529762-research-engineer).

**ET-16 — distinct propositions.** “50,000 evaluations across 155 countries” is a marketing claim about evaluation coverage. The disclosed validation population is 11,000 personas across the UK and US, and the working paper is a 7,755-participant UK study. No public language list or country/language/subgroup/question-family performance table was located. None of this proves or disproves performance in an unreported country or subgroup.

### ET-08 to ET-11, ET-14, and ET-15: deployment and governance

**ET-08 — deployment verified, contract/data-role layer partial.** News UK officially launched Times ExplorAItion on 27 April 2026 within Nucleus, initially across Times Media properties, as advertiser/agency decision support rather than a replacement for real-world research. Public sources describe subscriber behaviour, reader panels, engagement, PAMCo, and survey inputs, internal and advertiser-facing uses, and expansion plans. They do not disclose the contracting legal entities, price, DPA, or controller/processor allocation. The 10% holdout/642,000-subscriber/92% result remains vendor/customer reported and not question-level reproducible. [News UK](https://www.news.co.uk/latest-news/news-uk-launches-times-exploraition-synthetic-audience-insight-tool/), [case study](https://www.electrictwin.com/times).

**ET-09 — partial denominator.** The current homepage shows ten organizations under an undifferentiated “Customers and Partners” heading. Conservative single-state classification is: Atomico/LocalGlobe/Mercuri = investor; The Times = published case study with News UK confirmation; Virgin = named customer with reciprocal event material; MRS Evidence Matters = event participant; LSE/Wingstop/Sage/NYU = unresolved rather than customers. News UK is a published case; Lebara is named by News UK as already using the platform but lacked reciprocal confirmation in this pass; BP remains reported/unresolved. Historical first/last observation dates remain open.

**ET-10 — gap, not a null.** Declared indexed searches on 19 July 2026 covered Contracts Finder, Find a Tender, Digital Marketplace/G-Cloud, and GOV.UK using Electric Twin, Electric Twin Ltd, Electric Sheep Intelligence, company 15173006, Warner, Cooper, and Times ExplorAItion. No award, notice, listing, or grant surfaced. The interactive/bulk sources were not source-completely scanned. The only permitted statement is **no result in the declared indexed search**. A defensible null requires the full 28 September 2023–19 July 2026 bulk/API window and alias matching. [Contracts Finder API](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/apidocumentation).

**ET-11 — partial governance surface.** The Civil Service Commission establishes Simon Case’s unpaid, part-time role, approximately twice-yearly meetings, and restrictions through 31 March 2027 against privileged-information use, lobbying, using government contacts for influence/business/funding, and advice on UK-government bids/contracts. No public charter, complete membership, audit/publication/veto right, recusal/incident process, minutes, enforcement power, or removal mechanism was located. The present evidence supports low-frequency advice plus personal post-employment restrictions; it does not prove the board is ceremonial, empowered, breached, or deployment-approving. [Civil Service Commission](https://civilservicecommission.independent.gov.uk/case/member-of-the-ethics-board-electric-twin/).

**ET-14 — partial.** The 6 April 2026 privacy notice mainly covers website/service-user and sales-identification data, including Instantly/Leadsy, RB2B, and LinkedIn. It does not publicly allocate controller/processor roles for customer audience data, fixed retention/deletion periods, a product subprocessor list, transfer mechanism, re-identification controls, audit rights, or product breach procedure. Electric Twin says customer data is not used for general-model training or shared externally and reports ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification with a scope covering its platform, products, infrastructure, and engineering/operations. The underlying trust-centre certificate was not independently readable in this pass. ISO scope is not evidence of product accuracy, legal compliance, safety, or day-to-day adherence. [Privacy](https://www.electrictwin.com/legal/privacy), [FAQ](https://www.electrictwin.com/faq), [ISO post](https://www.electrictwin.com/blog/electric-twin-is-iso-27001-certified).

**ET-15 — governing product terms not public.** The public Terms page explicitly governs the website and says separate Product Terms prevail for products. No public product AUP was located for political persuasion, public-policy decisions, employment, credit, insurance, healthcare, children/vulnerable populations, discrimination, psychological targeting, surveillance, military/intelligence use, or classified environments; nor a public enforcer, review gate, suspension/remedy, or appeal. Capability marketing cannot substitute for permission rules. [Terms](https://www.electrictwin.com/legal/terms).

### ET-17 and ET-18: comparator denominator and fair provisional result

**ET-17 — still incomplete.** The Gartner artifact identity is fixed: *Emerging Tech: AI Vendor Race: Startups to Watch in Synthetic Population and Behavioral Simulation*, Vibha Chitkara, 14 April 2026, document 7718657. The report remains subscriber-only. Public reproductions recover **13 names, not the 33-company denominator**: Aaru, Arima, BluePill AI, CulturePulse, Electric Twin, Evidenza, Lakmoos AI, NewtonX, Qloo, Stravito, Unlearn.AI, Verve, and Yabble. Tier claims remain vendor-reproduced and the Gartner disclaimer defeats endorsement language. [Gartner subscriber URL](https://www.gartner.com/document-reader/document/7718657), [Stravito reproduction](https://www.stravito.com/resources/stravito-recognized-as-a-front-runner-in-the-2026-gartner-emerging-tech-ai-vendor-race-startups-to-watch-in-synthetic-population-and-behavioral-simulation), [BluePill reproduction](https://blue-pill.ai/blog/bluepill-is-recognized-in-the-2026-gartner-emerging-tech-ai-vendor-race-startups-to-watch-in-synthetic-population-and-behavioral-simulation-report).

**ET-18 — provisional five-vendor battery only.** Applying the same public-service, validation, customer, AUP/privacy/security, procurement, and geography questions to Electric Twin, NewtonX, Stravito, Verve, and BluePill produces three bounded observations:

1. Electric Twin is unusually richly documented on founder public-service lineage and sparse on public governing Product Terms/AUP.
2. Public validation opacity is common across this five-vendor subset; none exposed a full public protocol/raw result sufficient to reproduce headline synthetic-accuracy claims.
3. Public customer cases and enterprise-security claims are common. Verve is distinctive in this subset for publishing addressable use prohibitions, including political-influence and discriminatory/harmful-use controls.

These are provisional evidence-availability comparisons, not findings of motive, misconduct, superiority, or inferiority. ET-18 cannot satisfy its denominator-aware acceptance gate until ET-17 recovers all 33 watched companies or preserves the paywall as the final explicit denominator boundary.

### Next real boundary

The next pass should not add ceremony. It should exercise four concrete missing paths:

1. download and hash the complete Companies House filing set, then parse the 2025 confirmation statement/articles and 2026 allotments;
2. obtain the working paper PDF and preregistration directly, preserve their disclosures/methods, and request the exact NDAM equation plus question-level distributions;
3. run a source-complete UK procurement bulk scan across the declared company/alias/date matrix; and
4. recover the remaining Gartner roster from the subscriber artifact or record the inaccessible denominator without expanding ET-18 claims.

No candidate in this comment is ready for graph or publication promotion.

| Electric Twin | Website privacy policy and product FAQ | Personal data may be shared with unnamed service providers; vendor says it does not sell/rent personal data; product page says customer research data constrains broader underlying models and every new audience is benchmarked | model/provider names, model versions, cloud provider, region, subprocessor list, prompt/response retention, training-use terms, deletion mechanics, certification scope, version-change log |

| Stravito | Public site and trust/AI pages recovered by search | ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II marks/claims; Assistant says it works from client-owned data and cites sources | no public subprocessor list, provider/version/region map, prompt retention terms, or validation-rerun record recovered in this pass |

- Electric Twin privacy policy: https://www.electrictwin.com/privacy-policy

- `uses_model_provider`: **unresolved for all three**. Generic references to LLMs, API inference, or AI do not identify a provider.
- `uses_cloud_provider`: **unresolved for all three**. Trust marks and private-instance language do not identify custody or region.
- `data_region_claimed`: **not recovered**.

- `validation_rerun_after_change`: **not established**. Verve describes model-config logging/versioned fixes, and Electric Twin describes ongoing benchmarking, but neither public artifact pairs a named upstream version change with before/after validation results.
- `subprocessor_added` / `incident_disclosed`: no versioned public evidence recovered.

### Nearest boundary

The nearest missing artifact is not another inferred architecture diagram. It is a dated vendor-controlled dependency record: subprocessor list or DPA plus provider/model/version/change notice. Parent program: #30  
Related deployment dossier: #39  
Captured: 2026-07-19

### Operational test used

- **supplementation:** synthetic output is another input and observed human/performance evidence continues;
- **screening/acceleration:** synthetic output narrows or pressure-tests options before a live step;
- **partial substitution:** a named human-research round is omitted or compressed, while other human/observed inputs remain;
- **full replacement:** a named human-input process is removed from the workflow;
- **hypothetical:** capability language without a documented decision.

### Smallest real workflow path

News UK’s own launch describes Times ExplorAItion as a **decision-support** tool for testing campaigns before they go live and explicitly says synthetic audiences are not intended to replace real-world research or performance data.

Publisher source: https://www.news.co.uk/latest-news/news-uk-launches-times-exploraition-synthetic-audience-insight-tool/

An independent report quotes News UK’s commercial-services director saying human-led research remains the “gold standard” and that News UK does not want to replace it. It also reports that human reader panels and surveys seeded the system.

Independent workflow source: https://www.thecurrent.com/marketing/marketing-strategy-the-times-uk-ai-generated-audiences-media-planning-news-publishers

Electric Twin documents two internal workflows:

1. **Parenting channel:** synthetic conversations informed audience gaps, framing, naming, and visual branding; the vendor says work that would normally take weeks of qualitative fieldwork ran as a sprint **alongside other inputs**.
2. **Bonus accounts:** synthetic input shaped naming, communications, and the priority case for shipping.

Vendor source: https://www.electrictwin.com/blog/the-times-announces-its-new-synthetic-audience-tool-built-on-electric-twin

### Classification

- Overall advertiser workflow: **screening/acceleration + supplementation**. Live campaign performance remains a later observed step.
- Parenting-channel research round: **bounded partial substitution claimed by vendor** because a named qualitative-fieldwork function was compressed into synthetic conversations, while other inputs remained.
- Full replacement: **not demonstrated**.
- Decision authority: retained by News UK/Times teams; no automated decision authority is described.

The affected simulated populations include Times audience segments such as parents/younger readers and advertiser target segments. Public materials do not document notification to represented readers, an appeal/correction route, or a participant override. Those are **unresolved**; their absence from launch materials is not evidence of concealment.

### Comparison limits

A roughly tenfold time/resource saving is publicly attributed to News UK, but absolute cost, elapsed time, error, representativeness, and matched human-versus-synthetic results are not disclosed. The internal outcome claims are not a matched validation study.

### Nearest boundary / next real run

Obtain publisher-side protocols for the parenting and bonus-account decisions, including the human method actually omitted, other inputs, approval owner, validation against observed outcomes, disclosure, and correction routes. Until then this is one mixed workflow receipt—not evidence of organisation-wide replacement or democratic consultation substitution.

Acceptance remains **incomplete**; the workflow is classifiable, but no matched control or full substitution ledger exists.

I froze Electric Twin's 2026-02-11 accuracy page and reimplemented the only metric whose public description was sufficient for a basic calculation: https://www.electrictwin.com/blog/how-accurate-are-synthetic-audiences

The page defines 1-MAE as mean absolute difference between predicted and actual response proportions, subtracted from 1. A local arithmetic check using actual `[0.5,0.3,0.2]` and predicted `[0.4,0.4,0.2]` produced:

```json
{"MAE":0.066666666666666666,"OneMinusMAE":0.93333333333333335}
```

This reproduces the stated 1-MAE rule for a toy distribution; it does **not** reproduce Electric Twin's score.

### 2. Frozen claim ledger

| Claim | Public scope on page | Reproducibility from public material |
|---|---|---|
| 95.5% 1-MAE | vendor evaluation | metric rule described; benchmark data unavailable |
| 92% NDAM | vendor evaluation | normalisation purpose described, but no complete equation recovered |
| ~94% NDAM “same question twice” | human-noise comparator | underlying waves/sample unavailable |
| ~96% 1-MAE across eight traditional methods | opt-in, river, Prolific, MTurk and others | aggregation/baseline data unavailable |
| 11,000 unique personas | UK and US | dataset/question/subgroup ledger unavailable |
| average 20% NDAM improvement since launch | continuous evaluation; persona construction, post-processing, models changed | model/version series unavailable |

The page says held-out evaluation data is private and not on the internet, evaluation questions are excluded from persona creation, and post-processing/model inputs have changed over time. Those are useful method disclosures, but they also identify the public-reproduction boundary. No per-question distribution, subgroup slice, tail result, temporal cutoff, full model version, or downloadable benchmark was recovered.

### 3. Nearest boundary

Before comparative scoring, the programme needs the exact NDAM equation, frozen question/answer-option ledger, distributions or executable evaluator, model and post-processing versions, temporal cutoffs, and the eight-method baseline construction. Without these, `vendor_reported_score` is supportable; `replication_succeeded`, `baseline_outperformed`, and subgroup claims are not.

### 4. Rerun status

The same toy input deterministically returns 0.933333 for 1-MAE. The vendor's 95.5%/92% headline scores cannot be rerun from current public artifacts. Acceptance remains open; this is a reproducibility classification, not a validity verdict.

## First pass: standards baseline separates acceleration from employment effects

Parent: #30  
Captured: 2026-07-19  
Graph effect: **none**

### Smallest real path

Compared one concrete productivity claim and one explicit complementarity claim against current MRS, ESOMAR, AAPOR, and ICO materials.

### Task-level observations

| Observation | Classification | Evidence limit |
|---|---|---|
| Electric Twin advertises responses in 60 seconds rather than six weeks and quotes The Times saying the same team produced ten times the output | acceleration / research-volume claim | vendor/customer marketing claim; no verified headcount, budget, redundancy, or causal employment effect |
| Electric Twin says users can ask questions without survey design or panel recruitment | partial workflow automation claim | does not establish that sampling, interpretation, QA, advice, or sign-off disappeared |
| Verve says VIPS complement traditional research and reserves fresh evidence/lived experience/high-stakes validation for real people | assistance / selective substitution | vendor method statement, not independent workflow audit |
| Verve says senior researchers curate inputs, validate outputs, escalate contested items, and issue versioned releases | human accountability claimed | public self-description; no project-level audit packet recovered |

Vendor sources:
- Electric Twin: https://www.electrictwin.com/
- Verve VIPS FAQ: https://www.addverve.com/inspiration/faqs-verve-intelligent-personas-simulations-vips/
- Verve ESOMAR response: https://www.addverve.com/inspiration/verve-answers-esomars-20-questions-for-ai-based-service-buyers-january-2026/

No public redundancy, union record, statutory workforce disclosure, or matched pre/post headcount evidence was recovered in this pass. Therefore `redundancy_reported` and verified employment substitution remain **unestablished**.

### Professional-standard map

**MRS**
- The April 2025 AI guidance applies to MRS members and Company Partners alongside the Code.
- It requires synthetic elements to be clearly identifiable, transparency/explainability, participant notice where AI processes personal data in unexpected ways, and continuing privacy/data-protection responsibility.
- Source: https://www.mrs.org.uk/standards/guidance-on-using-ai-and-related-technologies
- PDF: https://www.mrs.org.uk/pdf/AI%2BRelatedTechnologies_MRSGuidance_April2025.pdf

**ESOMAR**
- The 20 Questions are a buyer due-diligence framework covering provider competence, practical failures, explainability, human oversight, training-data quality, security, ownership, and data sovereignty.
- This is a disclosure/evaluation framework, not evidence that a supplier complies merely because it publishes answers.
- Source: https://community.esomar.org/uploads/public/library/documents/miscellaneous/20-questions-to-help-buyers-of-ai-based-services.pdf

**AAPOR**
- The revised June 2026 Code states AI-generated responses/digital twins/synthetic responses are not research participants; cases must be identified as AI-created; “poll,” “survey,” and related terms imply human respondents; AI generation method, AI tasks, and human oversight must be disclosed.
- AAPOR membership is not certification of professional competence.
- Source: https://aapor.org/standards-and-ethics/
- Supporting guidance: https://aapor.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Responsible-AI-Integration-In-Survey-Research.pdf

**ICO**
- Synthetic data can preserve patterns of source personal data and is not automatically anonymous; purpose, lawful basis, minimisation, and re-identification risk remain relevant.
- Source: https://ico.org.uk/media/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/data-sharing/privacy-enhancing-technologies-1-0.pdf

### Accountability baseline

The standards converge on duties that survive automation:

1. provenance and clear synthetic-data labelling;
2. distinction between human observation and modelled response;
3. explanation of AI's task and limitations;
4. lawful basis, privacy, and participant protections where personal data enters;
5. human responsibility for design, validation, interpretation, and disclosure;
6. no competence inference from professional membership or certification marks alone.

### Nearest boundary and next run

The next real artifact is a matched workflow packet—not a generic jobs forecast. Select one completed synthetic project and one comparable conventional/hybrid project, then capture task hours, people/roles, cost basis, elapsed time, validation failures, corrections, and sign-off. Separately search official workforce disclosures for dated headcount/redundancy events.

Acceptance remains **incomplete**: the professional-duty baseline and claim taxonomy are established, but verified labour effects and matched workflow economics are not.

## Frontier screen: seven seams have positive anchors; none is promoted yet

Parent: #30  
Captured: 2026-07-19  
Graph effect: **none**

This pass tested all twenty frontier rows for the first promotion prerequisite: an addressable positive anchor. A positive anchor is not a finding and does not satisfy the rest of the promotion rubric.

### Promotion-packet candidates

| Seam | Positive anchor recovered | Why it is addressable | Remaining pre-issue requirements |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 data/panel supply chain | CACI says its 12-segment Fresco data engine is integrated with Verve VIPS in Fresco Live | named vendor, named data product, named simulation product, six-month POC | define complete source universe, licensing/data-role fields, and an ordinary non-integrated control |
| F-03 contestability | News UK names Times ExplorAItion, Electric Twin, advertiser-facing decisions, and visibility into inputs/assumptions | named deployment and decision-support process | identify correction/appeal/override routes and an affected-group/control case |
| F-06 healthcare | EMA documents Unlearn/PROCOVA qualification material; FDA meeting material records Unlearn's digital-twin method | named vendor, regulated method, named regulatory records | freeze regulated-product/method universe, health-data/privacy fields, and a conventional-trial control |
| F-08 finance | Principality Building Society and Verve publish a named first-time-buyer VIPS deployment for product/proposition work | named regulated-sector customer, vendor, population and decision domain | obtain customer-side governance, decision scope, consumer-impact boundary, and matched non-synthetic workflow |
| F-09 advertising measurement | News UK says Times ExplorAItion is built with Electric Twin from first-party and market-leading third-party signals; independent reporting names PAMCo inputs | named publisher product, vendor, advertiser use and data family | archive exact PAMCo release/licence, define JIC/currency universe, and distinguish measurement from simulation |
| F-10 standards/audit market | MRS, ESOMAR and AAPOR now publish directly applicable AI/synthetic-response rules or buyer questions | named standards bodies and current public documents | define conformity/audit scheme universe, enforcement predicates, payer/assurer fields, and non-member control |
| F-14 reseller/white-label integration | CACI and Verve jointly describe Fresco Live as CACI segmentation transformed by Verve's platform and sold to clients | receipted integration and customer-accessible combined product | classify prime/subcontractor/reseller/white-label role from contracts, name legal entities, and select ordinary direct-sale control |

Anchors:
- CACI/Verve Fresco Live: https://www.addverve.com/inspiration/caci-partner-with-verve-vero-to-launch-fresco-live/
- News UK Times ExplorAItion: https://www.news.co.uk/latest-news/news-uk-launches-times-exploraition-synthetic-audience-insight-tool/
- Principality/Verve: https://www.addverve.com/experience/principality-building-society/
- EMA Unlearn/PROCOVA record: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/other/response-list-issues_en.pdf
- FDA Unlearn meeting record: https://www.fda.gov/media/136577/download
- MRS AI guidance: https://www.mrs.org.uk/standards/guidance-on-using-ai-and-related-technologies
- ESOMAR 20 Questions: https://community.esomar.org/uploads/public/library/documents/miscellaneous/20-questions-to-help-buyers-of-ai-based-services.pdf
- AAPOR standards: https://aapor.org/standards-and-ethics/

### Hold screen for the other thirteen seams

| Seam | Verdict from this pass | Missing nearest artifact |
|---|---|---|
| F-02 likeness/IP | hold | named likeness feature, dispute, licence, or policy tied to a product |
| F-04 consultation substitution | hold | official synthetic-population procurement/deployment; generic government personas and synthetic-data guidance are not enough |
| F-05 crisis/resilience | hold | named synthetic-population programme, contract, exercise, or grant |
| F-07 employment/workforces | hold | named employer deployment of simulated employees/workforce |
| F-11 patents/public IP | hold | vendor-linked patent, grant, licence, assignment, or repository |
| F-12 liability | hold | enterprise/product contract terms tied to synthetic-population loss allocation; generic website terms are scope-ambiguous |
| F-13 incidents/AUP enforcement | hold | public incident/enforcement record or source-complete policy denominator; one vendor policy proves only a stated rule |
| F-15 acquisition/insolvency custody | hold | synthetic-vendor capital event plus publicly addressable data/model custody terms or notice |
| F-16 public records/FOI | hold | named public deployment plus retention schedule, FOI, audit or litigation-hold artifact |
| F-17 group privacy | hold | named dataset/deployment and documented group-level harm or regulator analysis |
| F-18 election law | hold | jurisdiction-specific legal source paired with a resolved named deployment/entity; #41's capability claims alone are insufficient |
| F-19 model drift/warranty | hold | named before/after upstream version change paired with warranty/accuracy claim and rerun state |
| F-20 concentration | blocked on dependency | frozen #38 vendor denominator and resolved legal entities |

### Why no child issues were created

The seven candidates have anchors, but the frontier contract requires all of: neutral selection unit, bounded universe, positive and negative/control anchors, symmetric rule, source plan, privacy boundary, forbidden-inference rule, and measurable acceptance test. Creating child issues now would convert source leads into premature obligations.

### Next same-path run

Draft the seven bounded promotion packets in this order:

1. **F-10** — standards documents and comparator bodies are already public.
2. **F-06** — regulatory records supply a strong positive anchor and clear health boundary.
3. **F-01/F-14** — one real integration can be examined under two distinct units without merging their predicates.
4. **F-09** — depends on exact PAMCo/data-licensing custody.
5. **F-08** — requires regulated-customer governance evidence.
6. **F-03** — requires a real correction/appeal/control route.

Each packet must still be accepted independently. Issue #49 remains an investigative queue, not evidence or publication narration.

## Full-program fan-out run: #31–#49 now have verified first receipts

Captured: 2026-07-19  
Graph effect: **none**  
Repository/PR changes in this run: **none**

The execution fan-out covered every bounded case and the frontier queue. Each issue comment was fetched back after posting. These are first evidence receipts and refusal records, not completed case packets or promoted claims.

### Receipt index

**State-to-market**
- [#31 No. 10/pandemic personnel](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/31#issuecomment-5016431494) — one ACOBA-backed transition row; no diaspora-rate claim.
- [#32 institutional succession](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/32#issuecomment-5016431685) — official GDS/CDDO/i.AI transfer/merger path; direct 10DS→i.AI succession refused.
- [#33 Faculty→Accenture](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/33#issuecomment-5016431889) — transaction control, personnel, Frontier product and CTO movement established; contract novation unresolved.
- [#34 pandemic infrastructure commercialisation](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/34#issuecomment-5016432136) — COVID-19 Data Store→competitively procured FDP successor path; no private-appropriation inference.

**Legitimacy**
- [#35 validator/adviser market](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/35#issuecomment-5016432386) — Electric Twin study classified as vendor-funded collaboration, not unaffiliated replication.
- [#36 Centre for Human Progress](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/36#issuecomment-5016430655) — filed shared-director surface only; no transaction/programme/funding link inferred.
- [#37 former-official portfolios](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/37#issuecomment-5016430905) — one official appointment/restriction bundle; monitoring and cohort completeness unresolved.
- [#38 analyst category](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/38#issuecomment-5016431262) — WEVO adds a fifteenth first-party public recovery; still not Gartner's 33-vendor denominator.

**Deployment**
- [#39 publisher corpus](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/39#issuecomment-5016431450) — News UK reciprocally confirms Times ExplorAItion/Electric Twin; data roles and publisher denominator unresolved.
- [#40 consultation/input replacement](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/40#issuecomment-5016431655) — mixed supplementation/acceleration with a bounded partial-substitution claim; no full-replacement result.
- [#41 political use](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/41#issuecomment-5016431563) — Aaru capability claims recovered; campaign legal identities/contracts/expenditure unresolved.
- [#42 government/defence](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/42#issuecomment-5016431849) — official NATO DIANA CulturePulse selection and UK Electric Twin surfaces; no award/deployment/clearance inferred.

**Technical/regulatory substrate**
- [#43 data lineage](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/43#issuecomment-5016432121) — real Times→Electric Twin input path; DPA roles, lawful basis, retention and anonymisation proof absent.
- [#44 metrics](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/44#issuecomment-5016432343) — published 1-MAE rule reproduced on a toy distribution; proprietary headline benchmark remains publicly non-reproducible.
- [#45 cross-cultural coverage](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/45#issuecomment-5016432548) — live 155-country/50k-evaluation claim does not reconcile to the detailed UK/US 11k-persona method.
- [#46 model/cloud/subprocessors](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/46#issuecomment-5016429997) — custody/security claims recovered, but named providers, regions, versions and validation-after-change are not public in the probe.

**Ownership/industry effects**
- [#47 capital/control](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/47#issuecomment-5016431469) — Electric Twin entity, PSCs, directors, allotment and rights-change chronology resolved; announced round economics not reconciled to filings.
- [#48 labour/standards](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/48#issuecomment-5016433405) — MRS/ESOMAR/AAPOR/ICO baseline and acceleration taxonomy established; no verified redundancy or causal employment effect.

**Frontier**
- [#49 frontier screen](https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/49#issuecomment-5016443220) — seven seams have named positive anchors; thirteen remain held/blocked. None was prematurely promoted.

### Cross-program result

The program now has **19/19 issue-level first receipts**, while case acceptance remains incomplete across the board. The strongest recurring pattern is not a network claim; it is a disclosure/denominator problem:

- category visibility is incomplete and vendor-publicity-biased;
- capability, programme selection and marketing routinely outrun award/deployment evidence;
- data/provider/model custody is less specific than security/accuracy claims;
- headline coverage and productivity claims outrun reproducible subgroup, version and workforce evidence;
- official filings often establish control events without resolving public funding narratives or operational rights.

### Controlling blockers

1. Authorized access to Gartner document 7718657 and the full 33-vendor denominator.
2. Source-complete public-service, publisher, deployment and comparator cohorts.
3. Customer DPAs, model/provider schedules, subprocessor histories and exact regions/versions.
4. Private benchmark data/equations and named before/after model-change validation.
5. Underlying Companies House filing PDFs for share-class/count/right reconciliation.
6. Counterparty-grade contracts, procurement awards, expenditure and customer-side governance.
7. Matched synthetic/conventional workflow packets and official workforce events.

No canonical claim, hop, score, chain, or graph effect follows from this run. The next phase should close these nearest boundaries case by case, then rerun the same acceptance tests before any cross-case recurrence analysis.

## Second pass: DPA and API-policy artifacts resolve legal-role and deletion fields

Parent: #30  
Captured: 2026-07-19  
State: `graph_effect: none`; preliminary, not promotion evidence.

### Baseline action

Reran the nearest missing-artifact path from the first receipt: search the public cohort surface for an actual DPA or customer-facing policy that allocates roles and governs customer inputs. This recovered two vendor-controlled artifacts outside the Electric Twin deployment probe.

### 1. Aaru DPA — resolved contract fields

Aaru publishes a Data Processing Agreement effective 2025-04-24:

https://aaru.com/policies/data-processing

Observed fields:

- Aaru is the **Data Processor** and the customer is the **Data Controller** for personal data processed in connection with the Services Agreement.
- Processing may include storage, access, analysis, and deletion, for the purpose of fulfilling that agreement.
- Covered people may include employees, customers, users, and others whose data is provided; covered data may include names, emails, contact data, IP addresses, and other identifiers.
- Aaru may not engage a subprocessor without the controller's prior written consent, and an approved subprocessor must receive equivalent obligations.
- Personal data may not be transferred outside the EEA without Chapter V safeguards.
- At termination, the controller chooses deletion or return; existing copies must be deleted unless law requires storage.
- The controller has audit/inspection rights.

This supports `processor_for`, purpose, rights-assistance, transfer-condition, subprocessor-authorisation, and termination-deletion fields **at the DPA level**. It does not name subprocessors, hosting regions, datasets used to build agents, or an anonymisation test, and the public page does not prove how a specific customer project was configured.

### 2. Qloo API privacy policy — resolved input-to-model-use path

Qloo's privacy policy, effective 2025-01-01:

https://www.qloo.com/legal/privacy-policy

Observed fields:

- Qloo describes itself as a processor acting on a customer/controller's instructions for customer data.
- It says customers must pre-anonymise API inputs and that it does not accept PII through API calls.
- API inputs are entity arrays and attributes; Qloo says it may incorporate anonymised entity associations into its machine-learning models to refine later output.
- It says it does not share individual customer arrays or clusters with other customers; output consists of generalized probabilistic inferences.
- Separate website/account data is governed differently: Qloo is controller, describes cross-border processing including the United States, and gives some retention periods.

This is a disclosed **vendor policy path**, not proof that customer input satisfies GDPR anonymisation or that Qloo cannot re-identify it.

### Nearest remaining boundary and rerun result

The retry materially narrows #43's blocker. Legal role and termination-deletion are no longer wholly undisclosed for Aaru; Qloo's API-input/model-use path is also publicly stated. The remaining acceptance boundary is deployment-specific: executed customer terms, named data sources/licences, actual subprocessor schedule and regions, project retention configuration, and technical singling-out/linkability/inference tests.

Acceptance remains incomplete; no inferred lineage edges were added.

## Second pass: named providers and retention rules replace generic dependency claims

Parent: #30  
Captured: 2026-07-19  
State: `graph_effect: none`; preliminary, not promotion evidence.

### Baseline action

Reran the first receipt's missing-dependency path against two additional public cohort vendors, requiring vendor-controlled customer/security artifacts rather than cloud logos or third-party architecture guesses.

### 1. Yabble — model and cloud providers identified

Yabble's vendor-authored security article (2023-07-28):

https://www.yabble.com/blog/5-data-security-questions-you-should-ask-your-ai-provider?hs_amp=true

Observed fields:

- Yabble says its AI solutions use **OpenAI** large-language models through an API and that it has an enterprise agreement with OpenAI.
- It says OpenAI does not use Yabble-customer API data to train OpenAI models or improve OpenAI's service.
- It says imported data is stored with Yabble, not OpenAI.
- It identifies **AWS** as an infrastructure partner.
- It describes multi-tenant operation with logical partitioning, encryption at rest and in transit, backups, and retention/deletion policies.
- It explicitly warns that its technology does not scrub imported data for personal information and asks customers to de-identify uploads.

This resolves `uses_model_provider = OpenAI` and `uses_cloud_provider = AWS` as dated vendor claims, plus a no-upstream-training and storage-custody claim. It does **not** resolve model/version, AWS services/regions, subprocessor schedule, exact retention duration, or an executed customer contract. Current product FAQs continue to state that platform data is not passed to OpenAI for model training: https://www.yabble.com/faq-yabble

### 2. CulturePulse ARES — named service providers and bounded deletion behavior

CulturePulse's ARES privacy policy, last updated 2024-04-01:

https://ares.culturepulse.ai/assets/Privacy%20Policy-Clh7ouHz.pdf

Observed fields:

- Named providers are **Amazon Web Services** for data storage and processing, **Hotjar** for website usage monitoring, and **Stripe** for payments.
- The policy says all ARES personal data is stored on AWS servers.
- A verified deletion request for personal or contractual-engagement data is to be completed within 30 days unless infeasible.
- General relationship data may be retained while the relationship exists and generally seven years afterward for stated business/legal purposes.
- Draft policy information submitted to the ARES Message Resonance function is described as not retained.
- Anonymised or aggregated personal information may be used to train machine-learning or AI models during the engagement.

This resolves named-provider, provider-purpose, general-retention, deletion-request, and one function-specific non-retention field. It does **not** identify AWS region/account boundary, model provider/version, backup-deletion timing, audit scope, or a versioned subprocessor-change event.

### Nearest remaining boundary and rerun result

The previous `uses_model_provider` / `uses_cloud_provider` gap is now narrower for these vendors. The next real boundary is a dated subprocessor schedule or executed DPA with regions and change notices, plus one named model/version change paired with before/after validation.

Acceptance remains incomplete: these are two bounded vendor custody paths, not a frozen-cohort supply-chain map, and no dependency edge was inferred beyond the vendors' own disclosures.

- Ben Blume is an Atomico investment Partner, while Electric Twin says Atomico led its $10m round.

Retrieve the September 2025 articles, resolutions and SH01 forms; then reconcile classes, counts, consideration, pre-emption changes, allottee identities and any nominee/observer rights. Until those underlying instruments are captured, round economics and strategic rights remain incomplete.

## Second-pass receipt: OSF registration recovered and inspected

**Parent:** #30  
**Captured:** 2026-07-19  
**State:** research intake only; `graph_effect: none`

### Baseline action

Queried the public OSF API for registration `6yqtu`, its contributors, and its registration storage:

- https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/6yqtu/
- https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/6yqtu/contributors/
- https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/6yqtu/files/osfstorage/
- frozen archive pointer reported by OSF: https://archive.org/details/osf-registrations-6yqtu-v1

### Observed protocol artifact

The registration is titled **“Comparison of different survey recruitment strategies.”** OSF records creation and registration on **2025-04-25**, prior to data creation, with an embargo ending **2026-04-01**. It is now public and accepted. Michael Muthukrishna is the sole bibliographic contributor exposed by the registration API and has admin permission.

The registered protocol is explicitly **exploratory**, observational, and unblinded. It specifies:

- the same questionnaire fielded eight times across opt-in, multi-source aggregator, novel opt-in/postcode lottery, river sampling, micro-task platforms, and AI responses;
- structured variation including high-/low-quality river quotas and repeated aggregator fielding at different times;
- **1,000 participants per sampling methodology**;
- about ten sociodemographic items plus political, social, and consumer questions;
- comparison of means and variances, regression tests, distribution comparisons including **CFst** and **Earth mover**, and a multiverse/specification-curve analysis;
- p-values, with postcode-block and attention-check exclusions included as analysis variations.

This materially upgrades the prior “SSRN reports a preregistration” pointer into a directly inspected registration receipt.

### File/replay boundary

The same OSF record reports:

```text
has_data=false
has_analytic_code=false
has_materials=false
has_papers=false
has_supplements=false
```

The registered OSF storage inventory is empty. Therefore the timestamped protocol is recoverable, but there is no questionnaire file, frozen input data, analysis code, result table, or executable replication package in the registration to rerun.

### Classification

The registration supports `credited_as_validator` and protocol chronology. It still does **not** establish `replication_completed`: the recovered design includes AI as one comparison arm, while the SSRN disclosure still classifies the published work as vendor-funded collaboration with adviser/equity roles. Protocol registration and unaffiliated replication are separate predicates.

### Nearest boundary

Retrieve the eight fielded instruments/data snapshots, AI model and prompt version, weighting/exclusion decisions, executable CFst/Earth-mover/specification-curve code, and deviations from this April 2025 protocol. Until those artifacts exist, the study can be audited prospectively but not replayed.

No repository, PR, canonical, or graph state changed.

## Second bounded findings receipt: Dentsu/Evidenza media-deployment chronology

Parent program: #30  
Builds on: https://github.com/BigBirdReturns/clifford-number/issues/39#issuecomment-5016431450  
Captured: 2026-07-19  
Graph effect: **none**

### Baseline action

Expanded beyond the News UK/Times publisher case and searched for a customer-controlled media-company source that names the synthetic-audience vendor, input system, workflow, and observed validation signal.

### New observed source family

#### 17 June 2025 — Dentsu + Evidenza strategic deployment

Dentsu’s official announcement says it partnered with **Evidenza** to integrate synthetic audiences into next-generation media planning:

https://www.dentsu.com/sg/en/our-news/dentsu-partners-with-evidenza-to-integrate-synthetic-audiences-into-next-gen-media-planning

Customer/media-company controlled facts:

- deployment surface: dentsu media strategy and planning teams;
- vendor: Evidenza;
- integration: Evidenza’s synthetic-research platform plus **dentsu.Audiences**, including dentsu’s proprietary **CCS panel dataset**;
- stated uses: audience insight, segment discovery, media planning, and movement from insight toward activation;
- reported early comparison: **0.87 correlation with traditional research**;
- reciprocal signal: the same Dentsu release carries a named statement from Evidenza co-founder Peter Weinberg describing the combined Dentsu data/media scale and Evidenza technology.

This is stronger than a vendor logo because the media company itself names the vendor and workflow. The 0.87 figure remains a deployment-party claim: the release does not expose sample, question set, holdout design, denominator, confidence interval, or independent validator.

#### 29 January 2026 — Dentsu launches Generative Audiences in the UK

Dentsu later announced a production capability called **Generative Audiences**:

https://www.dentsu.com/news-releases/dentsu-launches-generative-audiences-ai-powered-growth-intelligence-that-thinks-like-consumers

The official launch identifies the UK as the first market, says the system creates statistical simulations and synthetic personas from multiple data sources, connects insight to media activation, and is powered by **dentsu.AI** with integration into **dentsu.Connect**.

### Critical lineage boundary

The 2026 launch does **not** name Evidenza. Therefore:

- the 2025 Dentsu/Evidenza integration is a reciprocally signalled media deployment;
- the 2026 Dentsu Generative Audiences launch is a confirmed Dentsu deployment;
- continuity from Evidenza into the 2026 production stack is **unresolved** and must not be inferred.

This preserved break is material: a customer can move from an externally named vendor partnership to an internally branded capability without public documentation of whether the vendor remains, was replaced, or became one component.

## Second-pass receipt: candidate NDAM equation derived, tested, and kept non-authoritative

**Parent:** #30  
**Captured:** 2026-07-19  
**State:** `graph_effect: none`; no vendor score reproduced

### Baseline action

Started only from the vendor's public statements that:

1. `1-MAE = 1 - (1/k) Σ|pᵢ-qᵢ|`;
2. the worst three-option 1-MAE score is 1/3;
3. NDAM normalises the score to 0–1 regardless of option count.

Source: https://www.electrictwin.com/blog/how-accurate-are-synthetic-audiences

For normalized categorical distributions, `Σ|p-q| ≤ 2`. If NDAM is the **linear rescaling** of 1-MAE from its option-count-dependent floor `1-2/k` to `[0,1]`, algebra yields the candidate:

```text
NDAM_candidate
= [(1 - L1/k) - (1 - 2/k)] / [1 - (1 - 2/k)]
= 1 - L1/2
= Σ min(pᵢ,qᵢ)
```

That is the complement of total-variation distance / distribution overlap.

### Executed checks

A local arithmetic run produced:

| case | 1-MAE | candidate NDAM | overlap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| binary disjoint | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| three-option disjoint | 0.333333 | 0 | 0 |
| p=[.5,.3,.2], q=[.4,.4,.2] | 0.933333 | 0.9 | 0.9 |

The identity `1-L1/2 = Σmin(p,q)` held in all three tests, and the candidate removes the option-count floor exactly.

### Inference boundary

This is a **mathematically consistent candidate**, not `metric_defined_as` for Electric Twin. The public page does not state that the normalisation is linear, publish an equation, or expose evaluator code. Other transforms could also map the endpoints to 0 and 1. Therefore the 92% score remains `vendor_reported_score`, not a reproduced result.

### Current professional disclosure floor

AAPOR's final **Revised June 2026** Code now requires sufficient information for independent review and verification, including exact instruments/response options, population decision rules, AI-sample generation, languages, dates, human-response counts, weighting, limitations, AI task, and human oversight: https://aapor.org/standards-and-ethics/

That standard makes the missing equation and benchmark fields operationally precise; it does not prove noncompliance or invalidate a proprietary metric.

### Nearest boundary

Vendor confirmation or executable evaluator for the exact NDAM equation, followed by frozen per-question distributions, answer-option counts, aggregation weights, subgroup/tail tables, model/post-processing versions, and the eight-method baseline. Only then can the 92% and ~94% human-noise comparator be rerun.

No repository, PR, canonical, or graph state changed.

### Baseline action

Followed a matched cross-cultural benchmark from the paper to its public code at immutable commit `99e06a7cc3a084568105f37598009b239b18b858`:

- paper / COLM 2024 record: https://openreview.net/forum?id=S4ZOkV1AHl
- repository: https://github.com/louiskwoklf/llms-cultural-adaptability
- runner: https://github.com/louiskwoklf/llms-cultural-adaptability/blob/99e06a7cc3a084568105f37598009b239b18b858/scripts/experimentRunner.py
- model call: https://github.com/louiskwoklf/llms-cultural-adaptability/blob/99e06a7cc3a084568105f37598009b239b18b858/scripts/modelInteraction.py

### Exact recovered scope

The paper compares GPT-3.5 simulations with **7,286 human participants from 15 countries**. The code fixes:

- **15 countries:** Austria, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Israel, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Romania, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, UK;
- **12 prompt languages:** Dutch, English, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Italian, Norwegian, Polish, Romanian, Spanish, Swedish;
- model snapshot `gpt-3.5-turbo-1106`;
- `temperature=1`, `top_p=1`, `max_tokens=1`;
- a loop that runs every listed country under every listed language, i.e. a 15×12 experimental grid before participant filtering.

The reported result is a useful positive/negative control: explicitly giving country of residence improved alignment with human responses, while native-language prompting did not reliably transfer cultural fidelity and particularly reduced alignment for Greek and Hebrew.

### Replay boundary discovered in code

This is substantially more inspectable than a coverage headline, but the repository is not replay-ready as published:

- `experimentRunner.py` requires `../references/data/humanSubjects.xlsx`, which the README directs users to obtain from the Bos et al. source study;
- `modelInteraction.py` contains a blank API key and calls a retired/historical model snapshot;
- the checked-in `requirements.txt` is empty despite imports including `openai`, `pandas`, and Excel support;
- a live rerun would therefore not be comparable without the original human data, dependency lock, and archived model endpoint/output.

### Scope reconciliation

This benchmark supports the proposition that **country labels and prompt language are separate experimental variables** and that multilingual prompting can worsen, not merely improve, alignment. It does not validate Electric Twin's 155-country headline: different vendor, model, population, task, time, and metric. Nor do 15 countries imply 15 languages; the recovered experiment explicitly uses unequal sets.

AAPOR's final June 2026 Code independently requires disclosure of the population decision rules, geographic scope, language(s), dates, AI-generation method, and human-response basis: https://aapor.org/standards-and-ethics/

### Nearest boundary

For this benchmark: custody of the Bos human workbook, dependency/environment lock, archived prompts/outputs, and a model-substitution protocol. For the vendor cohort: separate country and language ledgers plus per-market validation, uncertainty, localisation, and abstention.

## Second-pass receipt: MRS toolkit yields a task-level automation/accountability map

**Parent:** #30  
**Captured:** 2026-07-19  
**State:** `graph_effect: none`; professional guidance, not employment-effect evidence

### Baseline action

Inspected the current **MRS Data Analysis and AI Toolkit (2026)** and AAPOR's final **Revised June 2026 Code** at clause level:

- MRS toolkit: https://www.mrs.org.uk/pdf/MRS_AIAtoolkit_2026.pdf
- AAPOR Code: https://aapor.org/standards-and-ethics/

### Task-level workforce record

The MRS toolkit makes a more precise division than a generic “AI replaces researchers” claim:

| Task boundary | MRS-described change | Evidentiary classification |
|---|---|---|
| participant recruitment/data collection | synthetic participants can remove recruitment and compress collection from weeks/months | task automation and speed/cost claim |
| cleaning and cross-tabulation | described as mechanical work AI can automate | role acceleration / partial automation |
| classification and findings | practitioners must review, validate, and correct outputs | retained human QA responsibility |
| demographic fairness | models require continuing audit | new/expanded audit work |
| segmentation or risk modelling | leadership must define human intervention/override points | retained governance responsibility |
| interpretation, forecasting, storytelling | analyst role shifts toward strategic work | role redesign claim |
| ethical/strategic validation | identified as a high-value human contribution | retained accountability |

The toolkit's conclusion calls AI a co-pilot and says human oversight and critical thinking remain crucial. This is professional-body guidance and a task taxonomy; it is **not** a measured headcount outcome.

### Final AAPOR responsibility floor

The now-final June 2026 Code—not merely the earlier proposal—adds enforceable professional distinctions relevant to synthetic work:

- AI-generated responses are not human research participants and must be identified as AI-created;
- “poll” and “survey” imply human respondents and should not label AI-created data;
- researchers must use fit-for-purpose methods, avoid unwarranted confidence/generalisation, correct influential errors, and disclose methods sufficiently for independent verification;
- immediate disclosure includes instruments, population, sample-generation method, AI task, limitations, and human oversight;
- membership/adherence cannot be presented as certification of competence.

These duties remain attached to practitioners even when recruitment, collection, cleaning, coding, or reporting is automated.

### Labour-effect boundary

No dated redundancy, verified pre/post headcount, payroll, union statement, retraining cohort, or matched project cost ledger was recovered in this pass. The strongest supported predicates are therefore `workflow_automated`, `human_signoff_required`, and `professional_code_applies`; `redundancy_reported` remains unestablished.

### Nearest boundary

A matched workflow with task hours and named sign-offs before/after adoption, plus separate official workforce records. Productivity and professional-role redesign must remain distinct from employment displacement unless that second evidence stream appears.

No repository, PR, canonical, or graph state changed.

## First receipt: CHMP qualified the statistical adjustment, not the upstream digital-twin model

Captured: 2026-07-19  
Parent: #49 / #30  
Graph effect: **none**

Official sources:

- EMA corpus index: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/human-regulatory-overview/research-development/scientific-advice-protocol-assistance/opinions-letters-support-qualification-novel-methodologies-medicine-development
- Final CHMP opinion: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/regulatory-procedural-guideline/qualification-opinion-prognostic-covariate-adjustment-procovatm_en.pdf
- FDA-hosted public-meeting transcript: https://www.fda.gov/media/136577/download
- FDA-hosted Unlearn slides: https://www.fda.gov/media/132612/download

### Smallest real regulatory path

The final opinion identifies a three-step procedure:

1. train and evaluate a prognostic model on historical data to predict control outcomes;
2. use the prognostic score when estimating prospective sample size;
3. estimate treatment effect after the trial with linear covariate adjustment.

CHMP's conclusion attaches to **PROCOVA as prognostic-score adjustment**. It says the procedure can increase power or precision in controlled randomized trials with continuous outcomes and that residual-variance reduction may be considered for sample-size reduction when uncertainty and other trial purposes are accounted for.

The opinion describes the implemented statistical method as a special case of ANCOVA with type-I error control and asymptotically unbiased estimates at sufficiently large sample sizes. It calls the prognostic-covariate procedure an acceptable statistical approach for primary analysis.

### The critical qualification boundary

The same opinion states that CHMP **could not qualify a formalized procedure for prognostic-model development in Step 1**.

Reasons and conditions recorded by CHMP include:

- only specific settings had been explored;
- useful outcome prediction cannot be assumed across diseases or future trials;
- external validity of historical data is paramount;
- historical and target populations may differ;
- model overfitting and optimistic correlation estimates require independent validation and sensitivity treatment;
- the precision or sample-size benefit cannot be generalized across therapeutic areas;
- nonlinear outcome models, treatment-by-covariate interactions, and some small-sample settings remain outside the qualified scope.

This produces a sharp component verdict:

| Component | Current verdict |
|---|---|
| linear prognostic-score covariate adjustment for in-scope RCTs | **qualified/acceptable with conditions** |
| upstream machine-learning or “digital twin” model construction | **not qualified as a formalized procedure** |
| a particular trained model's accuracy for a disease/trial | **case-specific and unresolved** |
| guaranteed sample-size reduction | **not established** |
| product approval, device clearance, or clinical deployment | **not established by this opinion** |

### Ordinary comparator recovered

CHMP does not identify PROCOVA as the uniquely preferred method. It directs applicants to compare:

- no adjustment;
- ANCOVA using ordinary prespecified covariates;
- PROCOVA using the prognostic score.

An attainable advantage over ordinary ANCOVA should be justified at trial planning. The opinion also warns that extra covariates or stratification factors already encoded in the prognostic score can create multicollinearity that outweighs the proposed gain.

### FDA authorship boundary

The 7 November 2019 FDA-hosted transcript records Unlearn's founder describing machine-learned “digital twins” that simulate a participant's placebo outcome and can be incorporated into trial control-arm analysis. That is a real public presentation at an FDA meeting.

It supports `presented_at_public_meeting`. It does **not** support FDA qualification, approval, or endorsement. The speaker and claim remain applicant-authored.

### Coverage state

- final CHMP opinion reached: **yes**
- regulator/applicant statements separated: **yes for this first document**
- ordinary comparators recovered: **three**
- upstream model-development qualification: **negative**
- disease/trial-specific trained-model validation: **inconclusive**
- complete six-document EMA manifest and hashes: **not yet complete**
- FDA regulatory decision concerning this method: **not recovered**

The newly important discovery is therefore not “regulators approved digital twins.” It is that one regulator accepted a bounded downstream statistical procedure while leaving the upstream prediction engine and each concrete model's external validity with the applicant.
